# tu 1.1.7 — installer puts tu on PATH for every shell

## What's new since `v1.1.6`

- **PATH is set up for you.** If `~/.local/bin` isn't on PATH, the
  installer adds one guarded line to your shell's startup file, picked
  from `$SHELL`: `.zshrc` (respecting `$ZDOTDIR`), `.bashrc` plus the
  bash login file on Linux, `.bash_profile` on macOS, fish's
  `conf.d/tu.fish`, or `.profile` for sh/dash/ksh. Missing files are
  created, so a fresh machine or Termux (which ships without any rc
  file) works too. Re-running never adds the line twice; it is marked
  `# Added by tu installer` for easy removal.
- **One line to paste.** The output ends with the single line that
  makes `tu` work in the current terminal (`export PATH=…`, or
  `set -gx PATH …` for fish), set apart by blank lines. New terminals
  need nothing.
- **Android (Termux).** 64-bit Termux installs the static musl build;
  32-bit ARM gets a clear message instead of a binary that can't run.
  Missing `tmux` shows the right install command for the platform.
- `--no-modify-path` / `TU_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` leaves startup files alone.
- **Update fixes.** A Homebrew symlink is resolved before deciding how
  tu was installed, and `/usr/local/bin/tu` is treated as an
  installer install rather than a `.deb`/`.rpm`.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hungryZoo/tu/main/install.sh | sh
```

Already on 1.1.3 or later? Press **u** in `tu`.
